data.name: Sri Lankan Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya Inaugurates Phase II Expansion of Adani Ports' Colombo West International Terminal Doubling Capacity to 3.2 Million TEUs
data.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ), in partnership with John Keells Holdings and the Sri Lanka Ports Authority, completed the USD 750 million Phase II expansion of the Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT), increasing its annual capacity from 1.6 million to 3.2 million TEUs and enabling simultaneous berthing of three ultra-large container vessels. The fully automated deep-water terminal, developed under a 35-year Build-Operate-Transfer concession, has already handled 2 million TEUs in its first 18 months of operations.

data.hook: President Marcos cut the ribbon on a new elevated expressway, promising drivers free passage through the end of 2026 to beat holiday traffic jams.
data.name: Marcos Opens NLEX C5 Northlink Segment Toll-Free Until 2026 End
data.summary: The two-kilometer NLEX C5 Northlink Segment 8.2 Section 1A connects Mindanao Avenue in Valenzuela City to Quirino Highway in Quezon City, slashing travel time from 40 minutes to just five. Marcos inaugurated the ₱2.2-billion project ahead of Undas holidays, joined by top officials, and declared it toll-free until year's end to ease congestion on local roads. It handles up to 11,000 vehicles daily and is part of a larger effort to link northern Metro Manila better, with a major ₱120-billion extension planned.

data.hook: Indonesia's new government has started redirecting natural gas from Singapore to power homes and businesses back home, a move that's testing ties between these close neighbors.
data.name: Indonesia Cuts Gas Exports to Singapore for Domestic Power Needs
data.summary: From October 24, Indonesia reduced gas exports by 31 million standard cubic feet per day from Natuna and Sumatra fields to boost electricity in Batam, Bintan, and Sumatra. Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong stressed honoring commercial contracts, while the Energy Market Authority said the cut affects less than 2% of daily demand and LNG can fill the gap. The city-state relies on gas for 95% of its electricity but has diversified to 60% LNG; observers note mutual dependencies, like Singapore supplying 40% of Indonesia's refined petroleum products.

data.hook: Indonesia redirected natural gas from fields in Natuna and Sumatra to power local plants in Batam and Bintan, leaving Singapore to tap its reserves.
data.name: Indonesia Cuts Gas Exports to Singapore for Domestic Needs
data.summary: Starting October 24, Indonesia reduced exports by 31 billion British thermal units per day to prioritize energy security for its own power plants and industries. Singapore's Energy Market Authority noted the cut affects less than 2% of its daily demand, with LNG imports and buffers keeping supplies steady. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong emphasized honoring commercial contracts, while some Singaporeans voiced worries over regional reliability and others in Indonesia defended the move for sovereignty.

data.hook: Women from nearby Kerala villages now guide massive cranes from air-conditioned control rooms, turning traditional port work into safer, inclusive careers.
data.name: Vizhinjam Seaport Transforms India's Shipping with Deep Waters and Automation
data.summary: India's Vizhinjam International Seaport near Thiruvananthapuram handles ultra-large vessels in natural 18-20 meter depths, cutting reliance on foreign hubs after starting operations in December 2024. It has processed over 2 million TEUs and 70 such ships in 18 months, powered by remote cranes and AI traffic systems that boost efficiency and safety. Recent moves include a $1.397 billion stake sale to Mediterranean Shipping Company and gateway services for local cargo, promising $80–$100 savings per container alongside community training and ₹75 crore investments.

data.hook: At Bogibeel Terminal in Dibrugarh, green flags waved as the DLB Patkai pushed off with 540 tonnes of methanol bound for Dhaka—a historic revival after nearly 70 years.
data.name: First International Cargo Ship Sails from Assam to Bangladesh Since Independence
data.summary: On October 5, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal flagged off the maiden post-independence international cargo voyage from upper Assam along National Waterway-2 on the Brahmaputra. The 1,300-kilometre journey to Pangaon Port in Bangladesh carries methanol from Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd, testing the river's role as a commercial freight corridor. Leaders hailed it as a boost for trade, employment, and eco-friendly connectivity in the Northeast, reviving a link dormant since the 1950s.

data.hook: President Prabowo Subianto has greenlit a review to reshape Indonesia's corruption laws, focusing on bribes over state financial losses—a move already dividing opinions sharply.
data.name: Indonesia's Prabowo Backs Study to Redefine Corruption as Mainly Bribery
data.summary: After a meeting at Istana Merdeka on October 20, National Economic Council head Luhut Binsar Panjaitan announced that Prabowo approved studying a narrower corruption definition, aligning it with the UN Convention Against Corruption that emphasizes bribery. Indonesia uniquely treats state financial losses as corruption, a stance Luhut says burdens state firms and investments by criminalizing business risks. Supporters see it easing bold investments, while critics fear it invites impunity, amid Prabowo's approval rating dipping to 44.5 percent over living costs and governance worries.

data.hook: The Department of Transportation shared before-and-after photos of a new covered walkway between two Quezon City malls, but many saw no real change—just a roof and some lights.
data.name: DOTr Completes Trinoma-SM North EDSA Walkway Amid Online Skepticism
data.summary: Announced on October 16, the project connects Trinoma and SM City North EDSA, aiming to shield commuters from rain and flooding on a busy route near MRT stations. First unveiled in December 2025, it includes a roof, lighting, and future links to the Common Station, all in coordination with mall operators. Online reactions poured in with sarcasm, like 'Ayun before and before' and 'wow… changes… groundbreaking…', as users questioned the subtle differences in the images and whether they truly show meaningful upgrades.

data.hook: Down 1-0 deep into the second half, Persib Bandung refused to quit. In just 10 minutes, they flipped the script with three stunning goals at Thammasat Stadium.
data.name: Persib Bandung Stages Epic Late Comeback to Beat Port FC 3-1
data.summary: Port FC grabbed the lead via a 66th-minute penalty from Jude Soonsup-Bell, confirmed by VAR. Persib equalized in the 87th through Mariano Peralta's finish from Balša Sekulić's pass, then Berguinho struck from distance in the 92nd and Luka Menalo headed home in the 96th for the 3-1 win. Substitutes and attacking flair turned the tide after a goalless first half, giving the Indonesian champions a perfect start in Group B of the 2026/27 ASEAN Club Championship Shopee Cup. Fans celebrated the resilience, with traveling supporters creating an electric atmosphere.

data.hook: Indonesia's deputy minister wants 70,000 Umrah pilgrims to fly straight to Saudi Arabia, bypassing neighboring stops for safety and homegrown benefits.
data.name: Indonesia Urges Direct Umrah Flights Skipping Singapore and Malaysia
data.summary: Deputy Minister Dahnil Anzar Simanjuntak recommended direct flights to Jeddah or Madinah to avoid risks from Middle East tensions and boost Indonesian airlines like Garuda and Lion Air. The guidance, shared after a meeting with travel operators, aims to strengthen the economy by keeping revenue domestic. Reactions vary, with some praising the safety and national focus, while others see it tied to tensions like haze from Indonesian fires affecting Singapore.
